meta.title: GitKittie Bud — Complicated git, made easy
meta.description: GitKittie Bud is a git client for Mac, iPhone and iPad: read history, compare any change three ways, and pick or undo exactly the lines you mean — on the Mac into your working copy, on iPhone and iPad as a pull request. Apple Intelligence drafts the words, on the device. In development.

hero.title: Change just the part *you mean.*
hero.subtitle: Read a repository's history, open any commit, and choose the lines that matter — then bring them back or take them out. GitKittie Bud does the git for you, shows you the result first, and always leaves a way back.

shot.alt: GitKittie Bud on the Mac: the sidebar, the commit graph with a merged branch, and the selected commit's files and diff.

showcase.title: Every change, *in plain sight.*
showcase.subtitle: The same calm navy window as Tasks and Folder, and one way of reading a change across the Mac, iPhone and iPad.

items.title: Pick the lines, *keep the rest.*
items.text: Double-click a commit and it opens in a window of its own: the whole message, every file, and the diff as Unified, Side by Side or the full file. Click the lines you want and put them into your files, or take them back out. Edits made since — even on the very next line — are kept.
points: Unified, Side by Side and Full File, with Ignore Whitespace
Choose a line, a range, a hunk or a whole file
History is not touched: the result is ordinary changes to review

shot.alt: A commit window on the Mac in Side by Side, with the analytics line chosen and Apply to Working Copy ready.

items.title: One commit that did three things? *Split it.*
items.text: Suggest a Split reads the commit's changes on your Mac and proposes separate commits, each with its own message. Use one and its changes are ticked and its message filled in; you confirm the split.
points: Drafted on the device — no key, nothing leaves your Mac
The same commit gets the same suggestion every time
You review every split before it happens

shot.alt: Suggest a Split on the Mac proposing three commits: a sign-up button, its style, and the remaining changes.

items.title: History and the commit, *side by side.*
items.text: Repositories, a branch's history and the open commit in three columns. Switch branches from the toolbar, pull to refresh, and open any file of the commit to read it.
points: GitHub sign-in, or a token for GitHub and GitLab
No clone and no git on the device
A demo repository to try it without an account

shot.alt: GitKittie Bud on iPad: repositories, the history of main, and a commit with three files.

items.title: Read any change, *anywhere.*
items.text: Every file of a commit reads three ways on iPhone too, with line numbers on both sides. Turn the phone for more room in Side by Side.

shot.alt: index.html in Side by Side on iPhone, the added docs and sign-up links next to the old navigation.

workflow.title: Undo one line of an old commit, *from your phone.*
workflow.subtitle: There is no working copy on iPhone or iPad, so chosen lines become a pull request: a new branch, one commit, and the request — nothing is written to the branch itself.

steps.title: Choose the line
steps.text: Open the commit, open the file, and tap the line that has to go.

shot.alt: The analytics script line chosen in index.html, with Undo and Bring to a branch at the bottom.

steps.title: Say where it goes
steps.text: Pick the branch, keep or change the new branch's name, and let Apple Intelligence draft the title and description.

shot.alt: Undo in a pull request: the target branch main, a new branch, the title, and Draft with Apple Intelligence.

steps.title: Review it as a pull request
steps.text: The change waits as a pull request for you or your team. Later edits to the same file are kept; if the line itself changed since, nothing is made.

shot.alt: Pull request #13 opened, with a link to open it on GitHub.

features.title: Point at commits, *not at flags.*
features.subtitle: Every verb applies to whatever you've selected: right-click it, use the toolbar, or press ⌘K on the Mac.

items.title: A graph drawn from real parents
items.desc: Branches occupy their own lane, merges fan out to each parent, and older history loads as you scroll instead of stopping at a fixed count.

items.title: Split a commit by what changed
items.desc: Tick the files or hunks that belong in their own commit and split them off into a new one, with its message drafted by Apple Intelligence if you like.

items.title: Pick and undo, line by line
items.desc: Bring chosen lines of any commit into your files or take them out on the Mac; on iPhone and iPad they become a pull request. Each file is merged three ways, so newer edits stay.

items.title: Always a way back
items.desc: Every rewrite needs a clean tree and saves a safety branch first, with a one-click Undo right after. Pushing rewritten history is its own step, with a lease, so it never overwrites someone else's work.

items.title: Pull requests in the same window
items.desc: On the Mac, read a pull request's files and patches, reply to inline threads and submit a review. On iPhone and iPad, list open, closed or all requests on GitHub or GitLab.

items.title: Apple Intelligence, on the device
items.desc: Commit messages, split suggestions and pull request descriptions are drafted by Apple's on-device model where it is available — no key and nothing sent anywhere. You can still bring your own provider on the Mac.

status.title: Where GitKittie Bud is today
status.text: The Mac app and the iPhone and iPad app are real and under test against actual repositories, but neither is on the App Store yet. Squashing, reordering and rewording older commits are being rebuilt on one rewrite engine before they ship.

cta.title: GitKittie Bud is *on the way.*
cta.subtitle: For Mac, iPhone and iPad. Be the first to know when it's available.
